paper.title: Federated Online and Bandit Convex Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Federated online convex optimization with first-order feedback, adversary class P(F^G, zeta)
unmapped: M machines with intermittent communication: R rounds with K local steps between communications (T=KR)
comparator in L2 ball of radius B (B_norm), shared across machines
bounded first-order heterogeneity zeta across machines (Assumption 1)
regret averaged over machines
settings.definition_quote: We consider the following distributed regret minimization problem on $M$ machines over a horizon of length $T$: \sum_{m\in[M], t\in [T]}f_t^m(x_t^m) - \min_{\norm{x^\star}\leq B} \sum_{m\in[M], t\in [T]}f_t^m(x^\star)

settings.name_in_paper: Federated online convex optimization with first-order feedback, adversary class P(F^H, zeta) (smooth)
unmapped: M machines with intermittent communication (T=KR)
comparator in L2 ball of radius B (B_norm)
average value at optimum F_star (small-loss quantity), non-negative smooth functions
bounded first-order heterogeneity zeta
settings.definition_quote: $\fff^{H}$, the class of convex, differentiable, and $H$-smooth functions

settings.name_in_paper: Federated adversarial linear bandits (one-point bandit feedback), adversary class P(F_lin^G, zeta)
unmapped: M machines with intermittent communication: K local steps, R communication rounds
comparator in L2 ball of radius B (B_norm); learner knows B and K
loss vectors beta_t^m in L2 ball of radius G
bounded first-order heterogeneity zeta (known to the learner for tuning)
settings.definition_quote: at each time $t\in[T]$, an agent $m\in[M]$ chooses an action $x_t^m\in\rr^d$ while simultaneously environment picks $\beta_t^m\in \bb_2(G)\subset \rr^d$. Agent $m$ then suffers the loss $f_t^m(x_t^m)=\langle\beta_t^m,x_t^m\rangle$.

regret counted at both queried points
bounded first-order heterogeneity zeta
settings.definition_quote: Function values of $f_t^m$ at two different points, a.k.a., two-point bandit feedback.

source.label: thm:first_lip
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{alg:NC_OGD} incurs an average regret of $\ooo\rb{GB/\sqrt{T}}$ against the adversary class $\ppp(\fff^{G}, \zeta)$, where $B$ is the norm of the comparator. This regret is optimal ... i.e., $\rrr(\ppp(\fff^{G}, \zeta), \aaa_{IC}^1) = \Theta(GB/\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Paper bounds average regret over M machines and T rounds; multiplied by T, so expression is total regret divided by number of machines N. Follows from serial OGD bound.

symbols.B_norm: radius of the comparator L2 ball

conditions: hard instance: coordinated stochastic linear losses with beta_t ~ (G/sqrt(d)) Unif({-1,+1}^d), same on all machines

source.label: thm:first_lip
source.quote: This regret is optimal against adversaries from $\ppp(\fff^{G, B}, \zeta)$ among algorithms in $\aaa_{IC}^1$, where $0\leq\zeta\leq 2G$, i.e., $\rrr(\ppp(\fff^{G}, \zeta), \aaa_{IC}^1) = \Theta(GB/\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Proof gives explicit average-regret lower bound GB/(2 sqrt(T)); multiplied by T. Holds even for linear losses, so also lower bounds the linear class.

tuning: step size tuned with H, F_star, B (Srebro et al. optimistic rates)

source.label: thm:first_smth
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{alg:NC_OGD} incurs the optimal regret of $\Theta\rb{HB^2/T + \sqrt{HF_\star}B/\sqrt{T}}$ against adversary class $\ppp(\fff^{H}, \zeta)$, where $B$ is the norm of the comparator and $F_\star$ is from definition \ref{ass:loss_optimal}.

results.notes: Average regret multiplied by T. Non-negativity assumed via Definition 2.2. Tuning may require knowledge of F_star; not explicit.

symbols.B_norm: radius of the comparator L2 ball

conditions: lower bound via coordinated stochastic adversary (P11) using construction of Woodworth & Srebro 2021 Theorem 4

source.quote: Consider the problem class $\ppp_{M,K,R}^{1, \sigma}(\fff^{G,B}, \zeta)$.
